title: ExtractEvent
description: One event of an Extract stream.

oneOf.description: The run started.

contract_version.description: The version of the contract it speaks, [`CONTRACT_VERSION`](crate::CONTRACT_VERSION).

oneOf.description:
A document's model output, sent before the document is committed. Store `json` and
send its path back in [`ExtractDocument::artifacts`] to replay it.

key.description:
What the output depends on, hashed: the text, the document's scope, the prompt, the
models and the section size. It names the artifact; a run replays every call any
artifact passed in holds, whatever its key.

oneOf.description: A document of the request's `remove` was taken out of the load.

entities_removed.description:
Entities deleted, left with no row creating them, no document naming them and no
fact.

facts_removed.description: Facts deleted, left with no evidence.

oneOf.description: A document reached its final state.

counts.description: What it put in the graph.

releases.description:
What the run did with each release decision of the request that names the document,
by its `decision_id`: written, refused and why, `missed` (the run committed the
document, and its commit held no review at that key and place) or `not_held` (the
load held the document already, with no such review: one a release wrote before, or
a claim this load never held there). `counts` counts reviews, of which one decision
may name several.

oneOf.description: The run ended; the result follows.

DocumentCounts.description: What one document put in the graph, or would have.

attribute_reviews.description: Property values the verifier was unsure of, written as reviews.

attributes.description: Property values it stated that were written as evidence.

attributes_over_entries.description: Accepted property values left out because its write had no room for them.

created.description: Entities it created, as its routes let it.

entities.description: Entities it names that resolved to the graph's.

identifiers_unverified.description:
Identifiers it gave entities that the verifier didn't accept, or that its text doesn't
write: none resolved an entity.

prop_conflicts.description:
Properties whose evidence now disagrees, with each other or with a row's value: each a
review.

rejected.description: Facts the verifier rejected, kept only in the artifact.

release_missed.description:
Release decisions of a document this run committed that name no review of it: its claim
has another key or place now, or the commit held no such claim.

release_refused.description:
Reviews a person released that stay held: an end no rung resolves, statements that differ
at one place, a statement other than the one approved, a value another statement disputes,
a `block` constraint it would break, or a review a release can't write.

released.description: Reviews a person released that were written as facts.

resolved.description: How its entities resolved, by rung.

unresolved.description: Names that resolved to no entity, or to several.

oneOf.description: It was committed.
No route reads its set: it was stored with its sections, and no model was asked.
The load already held it, by id and content.
The load holds the same text under another id.
It couldn't be extracted or committed.

retryable.description: Whether a later run may succeed.

oneOf.description: Its text, or its commit, is past a limit.
Its format isn't read.
A model call failed.
The store refused its commit.

replayed.description: Whether every model call it needed replayed from an artifact, at no cost.

usd_micros.description: The cost, in millionths of a US dollar.

ModelFailure.description: Why a model call failed for good, as the contract's model failures name it.

oneOf.description: The model declined the request.
The provider was unavailable, overloaded or broke off, retries included.
The provider refused the API key.
The key may not use the model.
The provider has no such model.
The provider kept limiting the rate of calls, retries included.
The account is out of credit or quota.
The request is too long for the model.

The model or endpoint can't do what the request asks (tool calls, structured answers),
or refused it as invalid.
The answer hit the output limit.

The answer couldn't be read: not the JSON asked for, or a stream that broke its
protocol.
The call ran out of time.
The model's weights changed since it was tested.
The endpoint resolves to a private address.

PhaseUsage.description: What one phase's model calls spent.

calls.description: Calls asked of a model, replays left out.

usd_micros.description: The cost, in millionths of a US dollar.

PhaseUsages.description: What a document's model calls spent, by phase of extraction.

adjudicate.description: Candidate assessment and independent identity pairing.

link.description: The link and attribute pass, gleanings included.

ReleaseOutcome.description: What became of a release decision.

oneOf.description: Every review it names was written as what it states.
Its reviews stay held.

The run committed the document, and the commit held no review at its key and place: the
claim has another key or place now.

The load held the document already, with no review at its key and place: one a release
wrote before, as a decision sent again finds, or a claim this load never held there.

ReleaseRefusal.description: Why a release decision's reviews stay held.

oneOf.description:
The document holds more reviews under the keys its decisions name than one read takes,
or the write was past what the store takes in one.

Its review keeps no statement to write: one of a property value, or of a load before
reviews kept them.
Reviews at its place state different things, and no word of a person's says which.
What its review states isn't what the decision's hash binds: not what the person read.

The document's model work states no such claim at that place now, as other artifacts,
models or prompts may read the sentence otherwise.
An end resolves to no one entity: a resolve decision settles the name first.

Its link holds one value and an end is linked by legal form alone: a resolve decision
settles that name first.

An end is linked by part of one row's name alone, whatever its link holds: a resolve
decision settles that name first.

An end is linked by an identifier the verifier didn't accept, the name the text calls
it by, whatever its link holds: a resolve decision settles that name first.
Its hold isn't one a person's word releases.

It conflicts with what the load holds of its link: a property of the fact that differs
from the one set, or a second object of a one-valued link whose slot keeps no statements
to weigh, as a load before P3 wrote it. An approval of a one-valued link's claim
otherwise outranks what it conflicted with.

It would open a `block` violation, or checking that needed more reading than the budget
allows.

ReleasedDecision.description: What a run did with one release decision of a document, by the backend's id of the decision.

outcome.description: What the run did with it.

ResolvedCounts.description: How many of a document's entities each rung of the resolution ladder resolved.

adjudicated.description: Linked by independently verified adjudication, when explicitly enabled.

alias.description: By another of its names, its fullest naming none.

identifier.description: By an identifier the verifier accepted, that a row gave one stored entity.

legal_form.description: By its fullest name without its legal form: a review lets a person overturn it.

own_name.description:
By an identifier the verifier held back without refuting, that is the name the text
calls the entity by and one row holds: a review lets a person overturn it, and it is
held to what a link by part of a name is.

part_name.description:
By its fullest name being part of one row's name, the rest of which only says what kind
of thing the row is: a review lets a person overturn it.

user.description: Linked by a settled resolve decision.
